rationale_overall: Filtered a large amount of noise this week: Blue Origin's New Glenn mishap coverage (Blue Origin is privately held, no investable ticker), a humanoid-robot marathon story out of Beijing (no identifiable US-listed vehicle), OTC/foreign uranium juniors (Traction Uranium, Uranium Royalty - excluded on liquidity/listing grounds), Peru F-16 deal and North Korea/Iran missile items (geopolitical color with no tradeable US ticker attached), Pakistani/Chinese satellite launches (foreign state actors), and a speculative Tesla/SpaceX 'Terafab' AI-chip megaproject story that reads as premature press-release hype rather than a confirmed catalyst. The one genuine signal was AST SpaceMobile's FCC authorization for a 248-satellite direct-to-cell constellation, reinforced by an FCC spectrum-capacity rule change - a real regulatory milestone for an early-stage satellite/space-communications vehicle. However, no current holding (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR) showed a matching removal catalyst this week: the RKLB 'up 250%, buy every dip' piece is bullish framing rather than a peak-enthusiasm sell signal, and SMR's earnings-anticipation pop is constructive, not a thesis breach. Per the swap discipline for this cadence, a single-week regulatory headline for a small, pre-revenue satellite name isn't yet 'clearly stronger' than an established holding, so the watchlist is held unchanged with ASTS flagged as a name to monitor for a future rebalance if it develops further evidence (revenue ramp, additional contracts).
